text:
nothing ages people faster than stress, idk if science agrees, but u damn sure see it compound over the years

that includes inability to cope w/ stress + unhealthy coping mechanisms (i.e. alcohol vs. exercise)

I'm told by guys age 50-60, that starting around age 50, you start seeing motherfuckers just drop dead

"mark died"
"the fuck do you mean mark died...he was just alive yesterday"
"yeah, he's dead"

and its usually the guys who were neurotic, constantly stressed -- where you can straightline how their mental health fucked up their physical health

are some jobs more stressful than others, yes...is there a huge dispersion in how people cope with that stress, also yes

Seneca/Plutarch must have written more on that topic than all the others combined. Cicero too

and its the same for relationships - the person u know who is always in drama, always high stress, angry, yelling and fighting

the last piece, and maybe the most important, is the recognition that avoiding toxic people is more important for stress than who u keep around u -- i.e. the absolute value of the negative > the positive.

the traits in people that drain you of energy, like envy, cruelty, resentment...slowly destroys u internally.

these traits have to be studied + uploaded so you know what to look for in people

it feels negative/pessimistic to dwell on, but its just the reality of managing stress

and the big dog was all over this:

I. "Munger’s overall philosophy was inversion-based: Identify what destroys lives (envy, irrational people, toxic environments) and systematically avoid it. He believed curating your circle — both personally and professionally — is one of the highest-leverage things you can do."

II. “If this gives you a little temporary unpopularity in your peer group, the hell with them,” Munger added.

III. Munger said of toxic people: "The great lesson of life is get them the hell out of your life — and do it fast."
